airport.name: Killeen Regional Airport / Robert Gray Army Airfield

summary: Killeen Regional Airport (GRK) is a joint-use civilian and military facility sharing its runway with Robert Gray Army Airfield on Fort Cavazos, one of the largest U.S. Army installations in the country. The airport primarily serves military personnel, contractors, and visitors to the Central Texas post, which was renamed from Fort Hood in 2023. Its location roughly 60 miles north of Austin makes it a convenient gateway for travelers heading to the Killeen-Copperas Cove metropolitan area.
faqs:
Q: Does Killeen Regional Airport offer commercial passenger flights?
A: GRK has historically offered limited commercial service, but its primary function is supporting military operations at Fort Cavazos. Travelers should check current airline schedules as service can vary.

Q: Can civilians access the military side of the airfield?
A: No, Robert Gray Army Airfield is restricted to military and authorized personnel only. Civilian operations use the shared airport facilities on the municipal side.

Q: What is Fort Cavazos known for?
A: Fort Cavazos (formerly Fort Hood) is a major U.S. Army installation and home to III Armored Corps, 1st Cavalry Division, and various training units, making it one of the busiest military posts in the United States.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Killeen?
A: The airport is located just a few miles from central Killeen and approximately 20 minutes from Copperas Cove, making it accessible for both military and civilian visitors.
transport_tips: Rental cars are the most practical option for getting to and from GRK, as there is no regular public transit serving the airport. The terminal is a short drive from both Killeen and Fort Cavazos main gate access points. Taxis and rideshare services are available but may have limited availability, so arranging ground transport in advance is recommended.
local_tip: If visiting Fort Cavazos, make sure to carry valid photo ID and have your visitor pass arranged through your sponsor before arriving—base access procedures can cause unexpected delays for first-time visitors.
